key_insight: VQE is generally not reliable as a ground-state preparer for QPE on fully connected Heisenberg spin-glass Hamiltonians, but its best overlaps do not appear to decay strongly with system size.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithms targeting molecular or materials energy estimation, this suggests VQE may still serve as a heuristic QPE preprocessor when exact ground-state preparation is otherwise out of reach.
method: Classically simulated VQE on disordered fully-connected anisotropic Heisenberg spin-glass Hamiltonians up to 15 qubits
Compared final energy and ground-state overlap as proxies for QPE-ready state quality
Tested ansatz depth effects, including more than three layers
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical evaluation showing poor VQE convergence overall, a correlation but not equivalence between low energy and high overlap, and no benefit from ansatz depths beyond three layers.
watch_item: Results are limited to a specific disordered Hamiltonian family and classical simulation settings, so hardware noise and broader chemistry-style benchmarks may change the outcome.
paper_title: VQE as Initial State Preparation for QPE on Heisenberg Spin-Glass Hamiltonians
